sources.title: GPT-2: 1.5B release
sources.evidence: Dated November 5, 2019. Announces the public release of the largest GPT-2 version and its weights, completing the staged release. Describes its nominal 1.5B model size.

sources.title: GPT-2 model card, November 2019
sources.evidence: Names the 1.5-billion-parameter model as the fourth and largest GPT-2 release, developed by OpenAI and trained on WebText. Describes a generative text language model. The February 2019 model date is distinct from November public weight availability.

sources.title: GPT-2 current published Modified MIT License
sources.evidence: The original developer repository currently publishes Modified MIT terms for code and models. The 2019 release used ordinary MIT; the Modified MIT wording was introduced January 3, 2020 and cleaned January 4. Its generated-content statements and notice exception should not be described as terms present at the November release.

sources.title: Original OpenAI 1558M hyperparameters
sources.evidence: Direct original-checkpoint configuration specifies vocabulary 50,257, context 1,024, hidden dimension 1,600, 25 attention heads and 48 Transformer blocks.

sources.title: Original GPT-2 model implementation
sources.evidence: Defines dense causal self-attention, biasful MLPs with fourfold expansion, learned position embeddings and layer norms. Output logits reuse the input token embedding matrix, so it is one learned parameter set. Causal masks and past keys/values are computed, not stored learned variables.

sources.title: Original OpenAI 1558M TensorFlow checkpoint index
sources.evidence: Read the complete 20,724-byte index only. All 580 F32 variables match every name and shape reconstructed from the original implementation and exact hyperparameters. Their shapes total 1,557,611,200 learned parameters. No quantization, optimizer state, stored masks, buffers or extra task heads appear. Offsets are contiguous and end at 6,230,444,800 bytes, matching a HEAD-only request for the original weight file. No weight data were downloaded.

sources.title: Better language models and their implications
sources.evidence: The February 14, 2019 announcement describes the largest GPT-2 model but explicitly withholds its weights while releasing only a smaller model. Text generation is autoregressive next-token prediction. This is evidence against using February as the public 1.5B release date.

sources.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
sources.evidence: The original technical report identifies the largest GPT-2 model as a Transformer trained on WebText and evaluated through text completion. General commonsense reasoning benchmarks do not define a dedicated reasoning mode. No separate active-parameter count or native structured tool interface is disclosed.

sources.title: GPT-2 complete license file history
sources.evidence: The complete file history has three commits: ordinary MIT added February 20, 2019 (aae26abd600ad32771fadf6284f339f07b9d8ea1); Modified MIT introduced January 3, 2020 (0f97760ebe1ccad5778a6d5957b2be9800e4efd8); wording cleaned January 4 (0574c5708b094bfa0b0f6dfe3fd284d9a045acd9). All three license versions were read. Thus the November 2019 1.5B release originally used ordinary MIT, while the current published license is Modified MIT.

name.note: Retain the original published size label for model identity; the exact complete count is recorded separately.

developer.note: The original announcement and model card identify OpenAI.

family.note: This is the fourth and largest GPT-2 release.

release_date.note: Earliest general public release of these weights. February announcement and subsequent selected-partner sharing did not make the full checkpoint publicly available.

open_weights.note: Original checkpoint metadata remains publicly readable from OpenAI storage, and the release explicitly includes weights.

license.note: Current published repository terms are Modified MIT. The November 2019 release originally used ordinary MIT; the license was changed in January 2020.

parameters_b.note: Exact complete learned count: 1,557,611,200 across 580 original F32 variables. Reconstruction: 50,257×1,600 token embeddings + 1,024×1,600 position embeddings + 48×(12×1,600² + 13×1,600) block parameters + 2×1,600 final norm parameters. All indexed names, shapes and storage lengths match. Tied input/output embeddings count once; no learned components are omitted. The public name uses nominal 1.5B.

active_parameters_b.note: No separately defined active-per-token count is disclosed. Dense architecture and complete parameter count do not justify substituting a total for an active count.

architecture.note: 48 dense decoder-only Transformer blocks, width 1,600 and 25 attention heads; causal attention and standard dense MLPs, with no expert routing.

context_window.note: The original checkpoint sets n_ctx=1024 and stores a 1024-position learned embedding table.

modalities.note: Original interface accepts tokenized text and returns text-token logits/generations; no image, audio or video modules are present.

reasoning.note: General reasoning benchmark evaluations are not evidence of a dedicated reasoning mode. The original release does not specify this feature flag.

tool_call.note: No native structured tool-calling protocol is documented. Do not turn absence of a feature specification into a categorical inability claim.

description.value: Largest GPT-2 checkpoint, a 48-layer dense Transformer trained on WebText for autoregressive text generation.
description.note: Replace generic staged-release wording with model-specific architecture, training corpus and function.

patch.description: Largest GPT-2 checkpoint, a 48-layer dense Transformer trained on WebText for autoregressive text generation.
patch.notes: Released publicly on November 5, 2019 after the February announcement withheld the largest model. The original 1558M TensorFlow checkpoint contains exactly 1,557,611,200 learned parameters; 1.5B remains its published size label. Tied token embeddings count once. Active parameters are not separately disclosed. The November 2019 release originally used MIT; the repository changed to Modified MIT in January 2020, which remains its current published license.

summary: Verified the November 5, 2019 public weight release, original dense 48-layer architecture, 1024-token context and text modalities. Replaced nominal 1.5B with the exact 1.5576112B complete learned count using only original checkpoint metadata and a full implementation reconstruction. Recorded current Modified MIT terms, distinguishing them from the ordinary MIT license used at the November 2019 release. Active count, dedicated reasoning and structured tool calling remain unasserted.
